docs.title: HospitalSim
docs.text:
HospitalSim is a hospital management system built with a React dashboard and a FastAPI CRUD API backed by MySQL. Manual forms, deterministic population, Testing, and Swagger all operate on the same records. Hospitals have patient capacity limits; staff records include admission dates, check-in times, and exact salaries; roles carry access classifications; patients show default or uploaded profile images.

Getting started Local dashboard Swagger API

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Launch the stack with Getting started. A new database starts empty.
  2. On the first startup, choose Start empty to add records manually or Pre-populate to review the fixed demo baseline.
  3. Use the Dashboard guide for CRUD forms, SQL previews, and the Testing sequence.
  4. Explore API usage, the Data model, and Architecture.
  5. See Development for checks and Troubleshooting for connection and validation errors.

docs.title: Showcase
docs.text: Watch the current Overview tour, or follow Recording and rebuilding to capture live CRUD and Testing workflows.

docs.title: Actual database operations
docs.text:
Populate restores two demo hospitals, three roles, three staff, and four patients. Test performs eight predefined CRUD operations and leaves five demo patients, with four assigned to staff. Each request commits to MySQL. The resulting values and relationships are repeatable; generated IDs may change.

Every dashboard request has an illustrative SQL preview. This is a demo example only: the browser sends HTTP and JSON, never SQL. FastAPI validates input and executes parameterized ORM queries. The preview shows what will probably run, rather than an exact SQL trace.

run.sh deliberately deletes Compose volumes and MySQL records to create a clean instance. See Getting started for preserving data instead.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The dashboard, Testing tab, and Swagger all use one FastAPI CRUD API and one MySQL database. Four domain models store hospital capacity, staff employment/check-in/pay data, role access classifications, and patient image BLOBs alongside their relationships. One additional infrastructure table, app_state, stores the database-wide startup flag.

Component Technology Responsibility Dashboard React, TypeScript, Vite API-backed views, manual CRUD forms, request/SQL previews Test plans web/src/demo.ts Fixed fixtures, ordered CRUD operations, baseline/final checks HTTP client web/src/api.ts HTTP/JSON requests, errors, response updates, illustrative SQL Frontend server Nginx in Compose; Vite locally Serve assets and proxy /api/* to FastAPI API FastAPI, SQLModel Validate requests and execute CRUD transactions Database MySQL 8.4 Persist hospitals, roles, staff, patients, and staff-role links Documentation MkDocs Material Guides and API/model reference

docs.title: Request path
docs.text:
A dashboard action shows its method, path, JSON, and SQL example before confirmation. The browser sends HTTP to /api/patients, for example; the same-origin proxy strips /api and forwards /patients to FastAPI. Nginx uses Compose's web:8080; Vite development/preview use 127.0.0.1:8080. FastAPI paths retain no /api prefix. Swagger's direct default address is port 8080.

Each router obtains a SQLModel session, validates fields and references, modifies model instances, commits, and returns a declared response schema. The dashboard updates from successful responses and reloads collections after manual mutations, population, and completion of a test. There is no polling or synchronization with other clients; use Refresh to read their changes.

SQL previews are illustrative demo examples, never executable browser input. The browser sends JSON, not SQL; the backend uses parameterized ORM statements and may execute additional queries. SQL_ECHO exposes actual statements in server logs.

docs.title: HTTP cache policy
docs.text: app/caching.py applies response policy through FastAPI middleware: private successful reads of roles (300 seconds), hospitals (60 seconds), and staff (15 seconds); patient reads and writes are never stored. Initialization, unlisted routes, and handled HTTP errors also use no-store. The dashboard sends all GETs with Fetch cache: 'no-store' to keep manual operations and deterministic checks current. The backend has no result cache or additional caching service. See API cache policy.

docs.title: Database-backed startup
docs.text: GET /initialization reads app_state row 1, returning was_initialized=false when no row exists. The dashboard also loads the four domain collections. If initialized, it opens Overview; otherwise it offers the empty/populated choice. Confirming Start empty or successfully verifying initial population calls POST /initialization, which uses a MySQL upsert to save true idempotently. This flag is shared across clients and survives application restarts. GET makes no writes; canceled/failed population does not mark success. A database volume reset clears the flag along with domain data.

docs.title: Deterministic orchestration
docs.text:
Populate resets only patients/staff in the two reserved named demo hospitals and restores their hospital/role definitions. Test requires that baseline and sends eight fixed mutations in order. Created IDs are taken from API responses. Resulting domain values and relationships are deterministic; auto-increment IDs may differ.

The test scheduler waits for one response before scheduling another request. Each operation commits independently and remains saved after interruption. Baseline/final checks use API collection reads; a preflight fingerprint catches changes since the confirmation preview. This is not a distributed lock, and other clients must not edit demo records during execution. There is no additional simulation model, server-side scheduler, or separate demo database.

The initialization flag lives in MySQL. The browser stores only loaded API responses, navigation, pending forms, the request log, and the current test cursor in memory. It does not persist domain records in local storage or invent fallback data. Reloading loses the execution cursor but retains MySQL changes.

docs.title: Deployment and persistence
docs.text:
The frontend image builds with Node 24 and serves static output in Nginx. VITE_API_URL defaults to /api; VITE_SWAGGER_URL configures the Swagger link. Both are public build-time settings. Static hosting alone cannot run FastAPI/MySQL. A separately hosted frontend needs an accessible API and a reverse proxy or explicit backend CORS configuration.

FastAPI's lifespan creates missing SQLModel tables. DATABASE_URL must use mysql+pymysql; MySQL is the only supported database. Compose waits for database readiness before API startup. /health reports process health, not a database query.

There is no authentication, pagination, or migration framework. create_all does not migrate existing tables. The db-data volume preserves records across normal restarts; run.sh deliberately removes project volumes to create a clean empty instance.

docs.title: Dashboard and Testing
docs.text: The dashboard opens without authentication. Its data comes from the FastAPI CRUD API and persists in MySQL. Documentation and Swagger links remain in the top navigation.

docs.title: Sidebar and appearance
docs.text: Clicking a sidebar destination, including the current one or the HospitalSim brand, scrolls to the top. The connection box is anchored at the bottom of the desktop sidebar and includes the MySQL/FastAPI and no-login details. Below it, a non-clickable local profile shows No login required and the visible Dark mode switch.

docs.title: First visit
docs.text:
On each page load, the dashboard checks GET /initialization and loads the domain collections. Until a startup choice is completed, the full-screen welcome page offers two choices side by side:

  • Start empty: retain loaded domain records and confirm saving only the initialization flag. A clean database has no domain records.
  • Pre-populate: immediately review the population writes against the loaded records, before any writes are sent.

Choosing Start empty or successfully completing Populate sends idempotent POST /initialization, storing was_initialized=true in MySQL. Refreshes and other browsers then open Overview directly, even if domain records are still empty. Canceling or failing initial population leaves the flag false. Resetting the database with run.sh clears it. Startup reads and illustrative SQL are visible in the loading/welcome screen and request log; a connection error is shown instead of browser fixtures.

docs.title: Manual CRUD
docs.text:
Use Hospitals, Roles, Staff, or Patients to create, list, read, update, and delete records. Create a hospital before staff/patients and roles before assigning them. Staff may have no roles; patients may be unassigned. Patient forms restrict clinician choices to the selected hospital and clear that choice when the hospital changes.

  1. Select Create record or Edit. The form shows a live HTTP/JSON and SQL preview.
  2. Select Review request, inspect the payload, and confirm Send request.
  3. The server validates and saves the record. All four collections reload from the API.
  4. Read previews a GET for one item; its response JSON appears in the request log.
  5. Delete has a separate confirmation. Referenced records may return 409 and remain unchanged.

Hospital and search filters work on loaded records and make no network requests. Refresh records previews and reloads all four collections. Use it after changes made through Swagger or another client. Metrics show patient count, assigned/unassigned patients, staff count, and hospital count. Care bars show each clinician's share of the loaded patient registry; they do not represent beds or capacity.

docs.title: SQL and request visibility
docs.text:
Every SQL preview is a demo example only. The browser sends HTTP requests with JSON, never SQL. The API uses parameterized SQLModel queries. Previews illustrate likely reads, validation checks, writes, and relationship changes; they do not promise exact SQL text, ORM ordering, or success. Enable SQL_ECHO=true to inspect actual SQL in API logs.

Previews show the HTTP method, endpoint, JSON body, and likely SQL. Named ID placeholders such as $riverside in JSON and :riverside_id in SQL refer to IDs returned by earlier requests. Numeric IDs are resolved before the request is sent. The request log keeps the latest 100 requests in memory and displays the latest 30, including errors and SQL examples. Refreshing the page clears this log, not the database.

docs.title: Populate
docs.text:
The Testing tab has Populate and Test buttons. Populate restores the fixed baseline:

Entity Baseline Hospitals [Demo] Riverside Medical Center in [Demo] Boston, Massachusetts; [Demo] Lakeside Clinic in [Demo] Cambridge, Massachusetts Roles [Demo] Physician, [Demo] Nurse, [Demo] Shift coordinator Staff Olivia Chen / physician / Riverside; Noah Patel / nurse / Riverside; Mia Brooks / physician / Lakeside Patients Alex Taylor / Olivia / Riverside; Sam Rivera / Noah / Riverside; Jamie Morgan / unassigned / Riverside; Casey Lee / Mia / Lakeside

Names, birth dates, role descriptions, and assignments are defined in web/src/demo.ts. Population deletes patients first, then staff inside the two reserved demo hospitals, restores or creates those hospitals and the three reserved roles, then creates staff and patients. Other hospitals and their records remain intact. Existing demo hospitals and roles keep their IDs; recreated patients and staff receive new MySQL IDs. Reserved role definitions are restored even if assigned elsewhere.

The main confirmation expands the planned database writes, including INSERT values and staff-role links, rather than leading with GETs. Supporting preflight and final collection reads have their own collapsed section. SQL remains illustrative and is never sent by the browser. The confirmation lists every deletion and creation. Do not keep irreplaceable manual records in the reserved demo hospitals. Initial reads detect changes since the preview; if anything changed, no writes are sent and an updated preview opens for another confirmation. Final reads verify the exact baseline. Repeating Populate yields the same demo values and relationships, with potentially different generated IDs.

docs.title: Test prerequisites and preview
docs.text:
Test requires an exact match to the baseline, including staff roles, patient assignments, hospital locations, and no extra patients or staff in the demo hospitals. If it is missing or modified, a popup explains the prerequisite and offers Review Populate. After population succeeds, the test preview opens for a separate confirmation.

Before running, review:

  1. The simulated story and expected final state.
  2. The ordered HTTP requests and payloads.
  3. The illustrative SQL reads and writes, including join-table changes.

The plan includes initial collection reads and final verification reads. The database is checked again before starting. Population is required again after a completed or partially completed test.

docs.title: Predetermined operations
docs.text:
Time HTTP operation Database effect 08:00 POST /patients Create Avery Stone at Riverside, assigned to Olivia 09:00 PATCH Jamie Set staff_id to Noah 10:00 PATCH Casey Set hospital_id to Riverside and staff_id to Olivia together 11:00 DELETE Sam Remove the current patient record, representing discharge 12:00 POST /patients Create Riley Quinn at Lakeside, assigned to Mia 13:00 PATCH Alex Set staff_id to null 14:00 PATCH Mia Replace role_ids with physician and coordinator IDs 15:00 PATCH Riverside Set location to [Demo] Boston, North campus

The final demo state has two hospitals, three roles, three staff, and five patients. Riverside has Alex (unassigned), Jamie (Noah), Casey (Olivia), and Avery (Olivia). Lakeside has Riley (Mia). Sam's record is absent. Unrelated records are excluded from these totals and preserved.

docs.title: Running controls
docs.text:
Confirming the test opens Overview with a top control bar. At 1×, a new request is scheduled three seconds after the previous step completes; 2× and 4× reduce that wait. Requests never overlap. Next hour pauses automatic playback and executes the next operation. Pause after request lets an in-flight request complete. Resume continues from the next step. End session stops future steps and returns to Testing; it does not undo committed operations.

Manual writes and refresh are disabled during an active test session, including while paused. Hospital filters and navigation remain available. On failure the test stops and preserves the log and committed data. No request is automatically retried: a timed-out write might already have committed. Refresh, inspect, and Populate before rerunning. Other clients should avoid changing demo records during execution; the sequence is not one database transaction.

The timer and cursor are page-session state. Closing or reloading the page stops scheduling further requests, while MySQL retains completed changes. There is no offline catch-up or browser-local data fallback.

docs.title: Additional record fields
docs.text:
• Hospitals: set maximum patient capacity when creating or editing. A full hospital rejects new admissions/transfers; capacity cannot be reduced below the current count.
  • Staff: enter admission date without time, optional last check-in including time (UTC), and salary using the numeric input with a 0.01 step. Salary stays a decimal string in the JSON request, preserving cents.
  • Roles: choose access type A, B, or C from the dropdown. These are stored hospital classifications; the application still has no login or permission enforcement.
  • Patients: the default profile is visible before saving. Upload a custom PNG/JPEG/WebP or use the default. The browser prepares a 256 × 256 JPEG from uploads and sends base64 JSON; the backend stores decoded bytes in a MySQL BLOB. Existing images stay unchanged unless replaced/reset. Demo patients have different coloured backgrounds.

Create/update previews include these values and illustrate BLOB writes with FROM_BASE64. SQL is a demo example only; the browser sends HTTP and JSON, never SQL. Salary, image, and date validation errors are returned by the API before any record change is committed.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Responsibility app/main.py FastAPI setup, router registration, startup table creation, health route app/database.py SQLModel engine, environment configuration, per-request session app/caching.py Central HTTP cache policy for successful reads and no-store responses app/models/ Table models and request/response schemas app/routers/ CRUD and relationship checks web/src/App.tsx Dashboard views, manual forms, request reviews, test controls web/src/api.ts HTTP execution, SQL examples, API response updates web/src/demo.ts Population/test plans, baseline/final state validation web/src/App.css / index.css Dashboard layout, styling, and responsive rules web/tests/ Node-based API client and workflow tests tests/ Schema, ORM, HTTP-cache, and optional MySQL integration tests docs/ / mkdocs.yml Documentation source and navigation compose.yml API, frontend, and MySQL services compose.test.yml / test.sh Isolated MySQL container and complete backend test runner

docs.title: Frontend checks
docs.text:
cd web
npm ci
npm test
npm run build

Tests use Node 24's native TypeScript stripping and built-in test runner. A mock HTTP contract checks repeatable baseline/final values, dynamic server IDs, request JSON, atomic patient-transfer payloads, preservation of unrelated records, prerequisite checks, partial failure/recovery, and null assignment behavior. These are client/workflow tests; they do not execute a real MySQL server or browser interactions. The production build checks TypeScript before bundling. npm run lint runs Oxlint.

For UI checks, verify the full-screen empty/populate choices, forms for all four models, request and SQL previews before confirmation, validation errors, keyboard/modal focus, narrow screens, Populate prerequisites, and pause/step/end controls. A failed write must stop the test without retrying. Refreshing must read persisted records without restoring browser fixtures.

The local Vite and Compose Nginx servers proxy /api to the backend. Test with the API running; there is no frontend-only simulation mode.

docs.title: Python dependencies
docs.text:
uv sync --locked

After an intentional backend dependency change:

uv lock
uv export --format requirements-txt --no-dev --no-emit-project --output-file requirements.txt

Commit pyproject.toml, uv.lock, and requirements.txt together. Docker installs the exported requirements; uv development uses the lockfile. PyMySQL includes its RSA extra for MySQL password authentication. The declared Python version is 3.14+.

docs.title: Backend validation
docs.text:
To run the complete backend suite against a fresh MySQL 8.4 container, install Docker Engine/Desktop and Compose v2, start Docker, then run from the repository root:

bash test.sh

The runner builds the existing API Dockerfile, mounts the tests read-only, waits for MySQL's health check, and executes unittest discovery with TEST_DATABASE_URL set to hospitalsim_test. No host Python, uv, or .env is required. Each invocation uses a unique Compose project with no published ports and temporary MySQL storage. Its test containers and network are removed on completion, failure, or interruption; all test data is discarded. The application stack and its db-data volume are separate. Docker retains reusable images and build cache. The command returns the test process's exit status; setup or cleanup failures also return a nonzero status.

For local checks without a database:

uv sync --locked
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

The database integration tests are skipped when TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset. To use an existing disposable MySQL instance instead of the container runner, follow the setup below.

Start an accessible MySQL database, export DATABASE_URL, and run the service. Use Swagger to exercise create/list/read/patch/delete for all four resources, including missing IDs, duplicate names, invalid dates, invalid references, and same-hospital staff assignment. Verify records persist across a service restart. Create an empty, disposable MySQL schema such as hospitalsim_test, with a user permitted to create and drop its tables. Run the API integration suite with:

export TEST_DATABASE_URL='mysql+pymysql://TEST_USER:TEST_PASSWORD@localhost:3306/hospitalsim_test'
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

These tests use MySQL only. They require an explicit TEST_DATABASE_URL using mysql+pymysql and a database name ending in _test; no application database is used as a fallback. The suite drops and recreates its test tables, so the named schema must be disposable. Without that variable, integration tests are skipped. They cover CRUD, references, invalid dates, null PATCH validation, protected deletions, staff transfers, shared-role persistence, and initialization across API clients. The independent ORM regression test runs without MySQL and verifies the role relationship is a collection: adding Mia must preserve Olivia's Physician assignment. The production lifespan is skipped so all table creation is controlled by the suite.

Required PATCH fields reject null with 422; protected deletions and transfers return 409. Commit-time integrity conflicts roll back. create_all is not a migration mechanism. Existing databases need the upgrade below, plus ALTER TABLE role ADD UNIQUE (name); if the earlier role-name constraint is missing. A deliberate reset with run.sh also creates the complete schema, deleting all existing project data.

docs.title: Linters
docs.text:
uv tool run ruff check .
uv tool run ty check --python .venv/bin/python .

Run uv sync --locked first to create the project environment. Ruff and ty are development tools. The optional media tools use Pillow and FFmpeg; live UI recording also needs Playwright. Their commands install tools on demand without adding API runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
uv run mkdocs serve --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8000
uv run mkdocs build --strict

The explicit port avoids conflicting with API development conventions. Navigation is declared in mkdocs.yml; add new pages there. Mermaid diagrams are supported through the configured SuperFences extension.

The GitHub Actions workflow builds and publishes on pushes to main. Configure GitHub Pages to serve gh-pages; the site URL is https://marcelopenas.github.io/HospitalSim/. Local edits or a source archive do not publish a documentation update automatically.

docs.title: Upgrading an existing schema
docs.text:
New databases receive all columns and constraints through SQLModel. create_all does not add columns to an existing table. Stop the API while upgrading an existing database, back it up, and apply the following MySQL 8.4 changes once. MySQL DDL commits implicitly; this is not a transactional migration. If you can discard the data, bash run.sh deliberately resets the volumes and recreates the schema instead.

First add nullable columns so existing staff can be backfilled with their real employment details:

ALTER TABLE hospital ADD COLUMN capacity INT NULL;
UPDATE hospital h
LEFT JOIN (SELECT hospital_id, COUNT(*) AS total FROM patient GROUP BY hospital_id) p
ON p.hospital_id = h.id
SET h.capacity = GREATEST(100, COALESCE(p.total, 0));
ALTER TABLE hospital MODIFY COLUMN capacity INT NOT NULL,
  ADD CONSTRAINT ck_hospital_capacity CHECK (capacity >= 0);

ALTER TABLE role ADD COLUMN access_type CHAR(1) NULL;
UPDATE role SET access_type = 'C';
ALTER TABLE role MODIFY COLUMN access_type CHAR(1) NOT NULL,
  ADD CONSTRAINT ck_role_access_type CHECK (access_type IN ('A', 'B', 'C'));

ALTER TABLE staff
  ADD COLUMN date_of_admission DATE NULL,
  ADD COLUMN last_check_in DATETIME(6) NULL,
  ADD COLUMN salary DECIMAL(12,2) NULL;

ALTER TABLE patient ADD COLUMN image_blob BLOB NULL;

The hospital backfill starts at 100 places, increasing it to cover existing patients. Legacy roles start with classification C. Review both values for your data. Set each staff member's real admission date and salary; last check-in may remain null. For example, replace the values and ID below with the actual data:

UPDATE staff SET date_of_admission = '2024-01-15', salary = 7500.10 WHERE id = 1;
SELECT id FROM staff WHERE date_of_admission IS NULL OR salary IS NULL;

The SELECT must return no rows before enforcing NOT NULL. Existing patient images can be backfilled using FROM_BASE64 and the shipped default icon; print the exact update from the repository root and run it in the chosen MySQL database:

uv run python - <<'PY'
import base64
from app.images import DEFAULT_IMAGE

encoded = base64.b64encode(DEFAULT_IMAGE).decode("ascii")
print(f"UPDATE patient SET image_blob = FROM_BASE64('{encoded}') WHERE image_blob IS NULL;")
PY

Then finish:

ALTER TABLE staff MODIFY COLUMN date_of_admission DATE NOT NULL,
  MODIFY COLUMN salary DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  ADD CONSTRAINT ck_staff_salary CHECK (salary >= 0);
ALTER TABLE patient MODIFY COLUMN image_blob BLOB NOT NULL;

Rebuild/restart the API and frontend together. Populate restores fixed values for all the new demo fields and distinct profile icons; it continues to reset patients and staff only in the two reserved demo hospitals.

docs.title: Full stack with Docker
docs.text:
Install Docker and Compose v2. From the repository root:

cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env to review development passwords and other settings.
docker compose up --build

bash run.sh deliberately deletes the project's Compose volumes and all MySQL API records, then rebuilds a clean instance. This is intentional for repeatable development and demonstrations. It exports requirements.txt with uv and creates .env from the example when missing. bash run.sh -d performs the same reset in the background. To preserve records, use docker compose down followed by docker compose up --build instead. The next dashboard visit offers an empty start or a separately confirmed population of demo records.

Component URL Dashboard http://localhost:3000 Swagger http://localhost:8080/docs ReDoc http://localhost:8080/redoc OpenAPI JSON http://localhost:8080/openapi.json Health http://localhost:8080/health

The database may take a short time to initialize. Compose waits for MySQL to respond before starting the API. SQLModel creates missing tables at API startup. The database is initially empty. The welcome page can leave it empty or populate a fixed dataset through the API.

docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f web
docker compose down

docker compose down preserves the db-data volume. To rebuild the web dashboard after changing its source or build variables, run docker compose up --build frontend.

docs.title: Local Python development
docs.text:
The declared minimum is Python 3.14. Install uv, supply an accessible MySQL database and user, then run:

uv sync --locked
export DATABASE_URL='mysql+pymysql://hospitalsim:YOUR_PASSWORD@localhost:3306/hospitalsim'
uv run fastapi dev app/main.py --port 8080

The API does not automatically load .env. Export the connection string in the process environment. The default Compose database has no host port mapping, so local Python cannot reach that database at localhost:3306 unless you explicitly add a mapping. Use a local MySQL server or a Compose override for that development mode.

docs.title: Local frontend development
docs.text:
With the API running on port 8080, use a second terminal:

cd web
npm ci
npm run dev

Open Vite's printed URL, normally http://localhost:5173. Vite proxies /api/* to http://127.0.0.1:8080 and strips /api. The dashboard requires the API and MySQL; it has no browser-local data fallback. npm run preview uses the same API proxy after a production build.

docs.title: Environment configuration
docs.text:
Variable Meaning DATABASE_URL SQLAlchemy/PyMySQL URL; required when starting Python directly MYSQL_DATABASE Database created by the MySQL container on first initialization MYSQL_USER / MYSQL_PASSWORD Application database user, distinct from root MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD MySQL root initialization password SQL_ECHO true enables SQL logging; defaults to false VITE_API_URL Public API base URL, default /api via same-origin reverse proxy VITE_SWAGGER_URL Optional public, build-time URL for the top Swagger link

For Docker, root .env supplies Compose interpolation and the frontend build argument. For Vite development, put VITE_API_URL and VITE_SWAGGER_URL in web/.env.local. The default Swagger link uses the browser hostname, HTTP, and port 8080. Set an explicit HTTPS URL when deploying over HTTPS. Never put secrets in VITE_ variables. Static hosting alone does not run FastAPI/MySQL: provide a reachable backend and a reverse proxy, or an HTTPS API with explicit CORS permissions. The API does not enable cross-origin requests by default.

Use URL-safe passwords or percent-encode special characters in a database URL. The example credentials are local development defaults. Existing MySQL volumes retain initialized users and passwords even after you edit .env; update database users explicitly when changing credentials.

docs.title: The dashboard cannot load records
docs.text:
Start the API and MySQL, then check http://localhost:8080/health and /hospitals. The dashboard does not generate browser fixtures when a connection fails. In Compose, Nginx forwards /api/* to web:8080; Vite development/preview forward to 127.0.0.1:8080. The prefix is stripped before the API receives the request.

Verify VITE_API_URL (default /api). Vite variables are embedded at build time; restart Vite or rebuild the frontend after changing them. Static hosting requires a reachable backend and a same-origin proxy or explicit CORS permission on an HTTPS API. The default backend does not enable CORS. A static frontend deployment does not deploy MySQL or FastAPI.

docs.title: Swagger does not open
docs.text: Start the API and check http://localhost:8080/docs. Set VITE_SWAGGER_URL for an external API or HTTPS deployment, then rebuild/restart the frontend. The default link uses the current browser hostname and port 8080.

docs.title: MySQL connection or authentication fails
docs.text:
Check docker compose ps and docker compose logs web db. Ensure root .env has all four MYSQL_ variables. Compose uses internal hostname db; local Python needs a connection string reachable from the host. The default database container does not publish port 3306.

A MySQL volume retains initialized users and passwords. Editing .env alone does not change existing users. Export DATABASE_URL for local Python; the app does not load .env itself. URL-encode special characters in passwords. Use the locked dependencies, including PyMySQL's RSA extra.

docs.title: Test asks to Populate again
docs.text: Test requires the exact baseline. A completed test, partially completed test, manual edit, extra demo patient/staff, renamed demo hospital, or changed role definition can invalidate it. Review and run Populate to restore the baseline, then confirm the test preview separately. Population resets patients/staff inside the two reserved [Demo] hospitals; other hospitals are preserved.

docs.title: A preview says the database changed
docs.text: Initial reads detected changes since the plan was reviewed. No planned mutations are sent in that case. The loaded data has been refreshed: reopen Populate or Test to review the updated plan. Avoid editing demo records from Swagger or another client during a run.

docs.title: A test stops or a request times out
docs.text:
Inspect the request log and API logs. Each successful request commits independently. Failures stop execution without retrying or undoing earlier writes. A timeout can occur after a write committed, so refresh and inspect before retrying. Review Populate to restore the known baseline for a new test.

Pause waits for an in-flight request to finish. End session and page reload stop future scheduling but leave committed records in MySQL. The execution cursor is not persisted; it does not resume automatically after a reload.

docs.title: API changes do not appear in Overview
docs.text: Use Refresh records and confirm its read preview. The dashboard shows the latest loaded API responses and does not poll other clients. Check the hospital selector and local search filter. All manual dashboard mutations reload collections automatically.

docs.title: A request returns 400, 409, 422, or 500
docs.text:
Use IDs returned by the server. Check the detail response and relationship prerequisites. Hospital names/locations and role names must be unique. Birth dates must be in the past. Patient and assigned staff must belong to the same hospital. To transfer an assigned patient, update both hospital and staff in one PATCH, or unassign first.

Null required PATCH fields return 422. Referenced-record deletions and staff transfers with assigned patients return 409. Unassign/reassign dependent patients or clear staff-role links before deleting their parents. See the API guide.

docs.title: Preview SQL differs from server logs
docs.text: This is expected. SQL previews are demo examples only: the browser sends HTTP/JSON, never SQL. The server validates requests and executes parameterized ORM statements, including additional relationship/validation reads. The preview is not an exact trace. Set SQL_ECHO=true to inspect actual backend statements.

docs.title: Startup fails after a schema change
docs.text: create_all creates missing tables but does not alter existing columns or constraints. Apply a database migration for an existing schema. Role-name uniqueness requires the constraint described in Development.

docs.title: Build versions or ports
docs.text: Use Node 24 and Python 3.14+. Reinstall with npm ci and uv sync --locked. Run npm run build for TypeScript checks. If port 3000/5173/8080 is occupied, change its configuration. After changing the local backend port, update the Vite proxy target and VITE_SWAGGER_URL; rebuild/restart as appropriate. Documentation development uses port 8000.

docs.title: Data disappears after run.sh
docs.text: This is deliberate: run.sh exports dependencies, executes docker compose down -v, and starts a clean instance. That deletes project volumes and all MySQL records. Use docker compose down and docker compose up --build without -v to preserve data. The next visit offers Start empty or a separately confirmed pre-population.

docs.title: API usage
docs.text:
The API is available at http://localhost:8080 in the default Compose setup. There is no /api prefix. Swagger UI, ReDoc, and the OpenAPI schema describe the running service.

Swagger's Try it out, the dashboard, and Testing all use these same endpoints and MySQL records. Use Refresh records in the dashboard to load changes made through Swagger or another client. The frontend's /api URL is a reverse-proxy prefix, stripped before requests reach FastAPI.

docs.title: Resources and methods
docs.text:
Replace {id} with the integer resource ID. The actual parameter names are hospital_id, patient_id, staff_id, and role_id.

Resource Collection Item Methods Hospitals /hospitals /hospitals/{id} POST, GET collection; GET, PATCH, DELETE item Roles /roles /roles/{id} POST, GET collection; GET, PATCH, DELETE item Staff /staff /staff/{id} POST, GET collection; GET, PATCH, DELETE item Patients /patients /patients/{id} POST, GET collection; GET, PATCH, DELETE item

All create/update payloads are JSON. Successful creates return the new record with status 201; list/read/update responses use 200; deletes use 204 with no body. PATCH applies supplied fields, rather than replacing the record. Lists return JSON arrays without pagination, search, filters, or an ordering guarantee. There is no PUT endpoint.

docs.title: HTTP cache policy
docs.text:
Successful collection/item GET responses use these browser-cache lifetimes:

Resource Cache-Control Lifetime Roles private, max-age=300, must-revalidate 5 minutes Hospitals private, max-age=60, must-revalidate 1 minute Staff private, max-age=15, must-revalidate 15 seconds Patients, including image data no-store Never store

Write responses (POST/PATCH/DELETE), initialization, health, unlisted routes, redirects, and handled HTTP errors use no-store. The policy is centralized in app/caching.py and registered once in app/main.py; endpoint functions do not repeat header assignments. Item policies match resolved route templates, including dynamic IDs and requests with query strings.

private permits browser storage and excludes shared proxy/CDN caches. must-revalidate prevents reuse after the lifetime expires without successful server validation; the API currently returns fresh responses rather than implementing ETags or 304 handling. These headers do not add a server-side result cache: requests reaching FastAPI still execute normal database operations. Other clients can see cached roles/hospitals/staff until their lifetime expires; updating an item does not automatically invalidate every related collection cached by other clients.

The dashboard deliberately uses Fetch cache: 'no-store' for every GET, including initial reads, individual reads, post-write refreshes, Populate/Test preflight checks, and final verification. Those actions always reach the backend and do not store patient data or reuse stale browser responses. Clients outside the dashboard can use the lifetimes above. The dashboard's loaded in-memory view and request log remain visible for the current page session; HTTP cache prevention does not erase an already displayed record.

docs.title: Create a complete relationship chain
docs.text: Create a hospital and role, then staff, then a patient. Example IDs assume a fresh database; always use IDs actually returned by your API.

docs.title: 1. Hospital
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/hospitals \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Demo Hospital","location":"Boston","capacity":100}'

{"id":1,"name":"Demo Hospital","location":"Boston","capacity":100}

docs.title: 2. Role
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/roles \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Physician","description":"Provides patient care","access_type":"A"}'

{"id":1,"name":"Physician","description":"Provides patient care","access_type":"A"}

docs.title: 3. Staff
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/staff \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"first_name":"Olivia","last_name":"Chen","hospital_id":1,"role_ids":[1],"date_of_admission":"2024-01-15","last_check_in":"2026-01-12T08:30:00","salary":"7500.10"}'

{"id":1,"first_name":"Olivia","last_name":"Chen","hospital_id":1,"role_ids":[1],"date_of_admission":"2024-01-15","last_check_in":"2026-01-12T08:30:00","salary":"7500.10"}

docs.title: 4. Patient
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/patients \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"first_name":"Alex","last_name":"Taylor","date_of_birth":"1990-05-12","hospital_id":1,"staff_id":1}'

{"id":1,"first_name":"Alex","last_name":"Taylor","date_of_birth":"1990-05-12","hospital_id":1,"staff_id":1}

Patient responses also include image_blob as base64; it is omitted from the short example above. The API supplies the default icon when the create request omits it. For custom images and reset semantics, see Patient profile images.

staff_id may be omitted or set to null at patient creation. When supplied, it must identify staff at the patient's hospital. date_of_birth is an ISO date strictly before today's UTC date.

docs.title: Read, update, and delete
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8080/patients
curl http://localhost:8080/patients/1

curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/patients/1 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"first_name":"Alexandra","staff_id":null}'

curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/staff/1 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"role_ids":[]}'

curl -i -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/patients/1

staff_id: null explicitly unassigns a patient; omitting it leaves the assignment unchanged. For staff PATCH, role_ids: [] removes all roles, omission or null leaves existing roles unchanged, and a list replaces the set of roles. Duplicate input role IDs collapse to unique relationships.

Delete dependents first: patients, then staff, then hospitals; remove staff-role links by updating/deleting staff before deleting roles. A referenced hospital, staff member with assigned patients, or assigned role returns 409 on deletion without changing those records. Unreferenced staff deletion removes its role links but retains roles. Integrity conflicts during commit roll back and return 409.

docs.title: Validation and errors
docs.text:
Status Typical meaning 400 Missing referenced hospital/staff/role; patient and clinician belong to different hospitals 404 Requested item ID not found 409 Duplicate hospital name/location or role name; protected deletion/staff transfer; full hospital or capacity below patient count 422 Invalid request schema, null required PATCH field, non-positive path ID, empty/overlong string, missing field, or non-past birth date 500 Unhandled server/database error; check logs

Router errors use an envelope such as:

{"detail":"staff_id and hospital_id must refer to the same hospital"}

FastAPI's 422 response has a structured detail array describing field validation errors. Check the actual response body instead of relying on status alone.

docs.title: Current limitations
docs.text: There is no authentication, pagination, or server-side list filtering. Testing orchestrates a fixed sequence of CRUD requests from the dashboard; the resulting domain records persist in MySQL, while the timer and execution cursor last only for the current page session. Hospital and role uniqueness are enforced by the router and database for new tables. Required PATCH fields may be omitted but reject explicit null with 422. Patient staff_id, staff last_check_in, and role description can be cleared with null; patient image_blob: null restores the default profile; null staff role_ids leaves roles unchanged. Every staff update validates its resulting hospital (400 if missing), including when roles are omitted. A transfer with assigned patients returns 409; unassign/reassign them before moving staff. Existing schemas require the columns and constraints in Upgrading an existing schema.

docs.title: Health endpoint
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8080/health

{"status":"ok"}

This confirms the process responds; it does not execute a database readiness query.

docs.title: Dashboard SQL previews
docs.text: Every dashboard request has an illustrative SQL preview. This is a demo example: the browser sends HTTP and JSON, never SQL. The backend validates requests and executes parameterized SQLModel/SQLAlchemy queries. Previews show likely checks, writes, and relationship changes, rather than exact SQL text or execution order. Enable SQL_ECHO=true and inspect API logs to see actual statements.

docs.title: Dashboard initialization
docs.text:
Endpoint Behavior GET /initialization Read the MySQL startup flag; no row means false; does not mutate data POST /initialization Idempotently set the flag true with a MySQL upsert; no request body

Both return {"was_initialized": true} or false as appropriate. This metadata is separate from the four CRUD resources. The dashboard checks it automatically on load, saving true after the empty startup choice or successful population. The flag survives restarts and is shared between browsers; only a database reset clears it. These routes do not populate or delete domain records.

docs.title: Exact field types
docs.text: capacity is a required non-negative integer. The API locks the hospital while counting patients; a full hospital cannot accept another patient. date_of_admission is required YYYY-MM-DD, and last_check_in is an optional ISO date/time stored in UTC as DATETIME(6). salary is required and limited to DECIMAL(12,2), including a maximum of 9999999999.99 and at most two fractional digits. Prefer a JSON string to avoid floating-point rounding; the response uses exactly two fractional digits. Role access_type is required and must be A, B, or C. Patient image_blob is optional base64 JSON for PNG/JPEG/WebP, limited to 65535 decoded bytes. Swagger includes these schemas and descriptions.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
SQLModel maps Python entities to MySQL tables. Create, read, and update schemas live beside each table model in app/models/. Integer primary keys are generated by the database.

erDiagram
    HOSPITAL ||--o{ STAFF : employs
    HOSPITAL ||--o{ PATIENT : receives
    STAFF o|--o{ PATIENT : treats
    STAFF ||--o{ STAFF_ROLES : has
    ROLE ||--o{ STAFF_ROLES : assigned
Model Table Main fields Relationships Hospital hospital id, name, location, capacity Many staff and patients Patient patient id, first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, hospital_id, staff_id, image_blob One hospital; optional staff Staff staff id, first_name, last_name, date_of_admission, last_check_in, salary, hospital_id One hospital; many patients and roles Role role id, name, description, access_type Many staff through staff_roles StaffRoleLink staff_roles staff_id, role_id Composite primary key and two foreign keys

The API serializes staff roles as a role_ids list rather than embedding Role objects. Relationships are not recursively included in read responses.

The dashboard uses these same fields and relationships. There are no bed, department, admission-status, or queue columns. In Testing, an admission is a patient POST, a discharge removes the current patient record with DELETE, and a transfer updates hospital and clinician together with PATCH. See Architecture.

docs.title: Relational model diagram (MySQL Workbench style)
docs.text:
The conceptual relationships above are complemented by this physical relational diagram. It includes the current MySQL column types, primary/foreign keys, nullability, the composite key in staff_roles, and the separate startup metadata table.

Open the full-size relational diagram

Gold keys identify primary-key columns; blue diamonds identify foreign keys. Filled dots mean NOT NULL and open dots mean nullable. Dashed connectors are non-identifying relationships; solid connectors identify the foreign keys that form the join table's composite primary key. Crow's feet indicate many, circles indicate optional participation, and bars indicate one. The staff_id relationship on patient is optional.

NUMERIC(12,2) is stored as MySQL DECIMAL(12,2), and MySQL represents boolean values as TINYINT(1). Capacity limits and the same-hospital clinician rule are enforced by the API; the diagram shows the structural relationships.

docs.title: Application metadata
docs.text: app_state is separate from the domain model. Row 1 stores the boolean was_initialized flag used by /initialization to remember the startup choice across browsers and restarts. A missing row means false. Startup table creation adds this new table to an existing database without altering domain records.

docs.title: Hospital
docs.text:
A hospital is the parent facility for staff and patients. Defined in app/models/hospital.py; managed through /hospitals.

Field Type Required on create Validation id integer Generated Primary key, read-only in API payloads name string Yes 1–200 characters; unique location string Yes 1–500 characters; unique capacity integer (MySQL INT) Yes 0–2147483647; maximum patient count

Location is free text; it is not parsed or verified as a postal address. Name and location each have separate database uniqueness constraints and router-level conflict checks.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: A hospital has many staff and patients. Each of those records references one hospital through hospital_id. Hospital responses contain only id, name, location, and capacity, without embedded relationship arrays.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{"name":"Riverside Medical Center","location":"Boston, Massachusetts","capacity":100}

PATCH may supply name, location, or capacity. The API returns 409 for admissions/transfers into a full hospital or for lowering capacity below its current patient count. Zero capacity blocks admissions. Patient writes and capacity updates lock the hospital row while checking the count, so concurrent admissions cannot claim the same final slot. Omit unchanged fields and do not set required values to null. A missing item returns 404 and a detected duplicate returns 409. Deleting a hospital with staff or patients returns 409. Remove or move those dependents first. Explicit null in a required PATCH field returns 422.

docs.title: Patient
docs.text:
A patient belongs to one hospital and can optionally be assigned a staff member. Defined in app/models/patient.py; managed through /patients.

Field Type Required on create Validation id integer Generated Primary key first_name string Yes 1–100 characters last_name string Yes 1–100 characters date_of_birth ISO date Yes Strictly before the current UTC date hospital_id integer Yes Must identify an existing hospital staff_id integer or null No If present, existing staff in the same hospital image_blob MySQL BLOB; base64 string in JSON No PNG, JPEG, or WebP, up to 65535 decoded bytes; default profile icon if omitted/null

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "first_name":"Alex",
  "last_name":"Taylor",
  "date_of_birth":"1990-05-12",
  "hospital_id":1,
  "staff_id":1
}

The read schema returns these fields plus the generated id, including image_blob as a base64 string. The example above omits the optional image; the API response additionally contains the generated default profile bytes. It does not include medical history, diagnosis, beds, departments, admission status, or treatment records.

docs.title: Profile images
docs.text:
The Patients form shows the default profile immediately. Upload custom image is optional: choose PNG, JPEG, or WebP up to 5 MB. The browser centre-crops and prepares a 256 × 256 JPEG, then sends base64 through the normal JSON POST/PATCH confirmation. The API validates base64, size, and supported image headers, decodes it, and stores binary bytes in a BLOB. Direct API clients must send at most 65535 decoded bytes, without a data:image/...;base64, prefix.

Omit image_blob in PATCH to keep it; null restores the default icon. Use default profile resets the form preview. Demo patients share the same generic silhouette with distinct coloured backgrounds, including the two patients admitted by Test. Images appear in both the directory and Overview patient registry.

docs.title: Updates and relationships
docs.text:
Omit staff_id in PATCH to retain the current assignment; set it to null to unassign. When moving a patient, update hospital_id and provide compatible staff_id in the same request, or unassign the staff member. The router checks the resulting patient/hospital/staff combination on create and update.

A nonexistent referenced hospital or staff member, or a cross-hospital assignment, returns 400. A missing patient returns 404; an invalid birth date or image returns 422. Admission or transfer into a hospital at capacity returns 409, without moving or creating the patient. Editing a patient already at that hospital does not consume another place. Required fields should never be explicitly set to null in PATCH.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Roles describe staff occupations or responsibilities and carry a one-character hospital access classification. The classification is metadata; the API remains unauthenticated and does not enforce these codes as permissions. Defined in app/models/role.py; managed through /roles.

Field Type Required on create Validation id integer Generated Primary key name string Yes 1–100 characters description string or null No At most 500 characters access_type MySQL CHAR(1) Yes Exactly A, B, or C

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{"name":"Physician","description":"Provides clinical care","access_type":"A"}

The router rejects duplicate names with 409 when creating or renaming roles. New tables also enforce role-name uniqueness in MySQL. Existing tables need the unique constraint described in the development guide. Missing role IDs return 404.

docs.title: Staff relationships
docs.text: Staff and roles have a many-to-many relationship through StaffRoleLink, stored in staff_roles with composite primary key (staff_id, role_id). Assign and remove roles through a staff member's role_ids field. An assigned role returns 409 on deletion; clear related assignments first. Role PATCH permits description: null to clear the optional description; keep name and access_type non-null. An access code outside A/B/C returns 422. The database also checks the allowed codes.

docs.title: Staff
docs.text:
A staff member belongs to a hospital, can have multiple roles, and can be assigned patients. Defined in app/models/staff.py; managed through /staff.

Field Type Required on create Validation id integer Generated Primary key first_name string Yes 1–100 characters last_name string Yes 1–100 characters date_of_admission MySQL DATE Yes YYYY-MM-DD, with no time component last_check_in MySQL DATETIME(6) or null No UTC date and time; null means no recorded check-in salary MySQL DECIMAL(12,2) / NUMERIC(12,2) Yes 0–9999999999.99; at most 2 decimal places hospital_id integer Yes Existing hospital checked on create and update role_ids integer array No Defaults to []; referenced roles must exist

role_ids is a create/update/read schema field, not a column in staff. The ORM stores relationships through staff_roles. Read responses return sorted role IDs. There is no singular role field.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "first_name":"Olivia",
  "last_name":"Chen",
  "date_of_admission":"2024-01-15",
  "last_check_in":"2026-01-12T08:30:00",
  "salary":"7500.10",
  "hospital_id":1,
  "role_ids":[1,2]
}

Salary is an exact decimal amount, not a floating-point column. Send a JSON decimal string (for example "7500.10"); responses always return a string with two decimal places. Currency and pay period are not prescribed. Invalid precision, negative amounts, and amounts exceeding the column range return 422.

Check-in inputs without an offset are interpreted as UTC. Offset-aware inputs are converted to UTC before storage; read responses omit the offset. Microseconds are retained by DATETIME(6). The dashboard labels the date/time input as UTC. PATCH with last_check_in: null clears it, while omission retains it. Admission date and salary are required and reject null.

docs.title: Role updates
docs.text: PATCH with role_ids: [1,2] replaces current roles. role_ids: [] clears them. Omitting the field or setting it to null leaves roles unchanged. Duplicate IDs are deduplicated through the relationship query. Invalid role references return 400.

docs.title: Relationship limitations
docs.text: The resulting hospital is validated on every update, even without role changes. Transfers to a different hospital and deletions return 409 while patients remain assigned. Unassign/reassign patients first. Required fields reject explicit null with 422; a failed validation leaves staff fields and roles unchanged.

docs.title: Current dashboard Overview
docs.text:
This 54-second tour uses the dashboard screenshot supplied with this version. Camera movement highlights the navigation, metrics, care assignments, Testing entry point, patient profiles, appearance controls, and documentation links. It does not record browser clicks, CRUD operations, or a running test.

Your browser can download the video using the link below.

MP4 video · Animated GIF · Timestamped JSON · Source screenshot

The timeline records each frame's timestamp, file path, caption, and camera crop. Its source metadata identifies the supplied screenshot and its SHA-256 digest. Rebuilding this tour sends no API requests.

docs.title: Live workflow recordings
docs.text:
The optional recorder drives a fresh local instance through:

  • Start empty and the welcome Pre-populate preview.
  • Hospital, role, staff, and patient CRUD forms, individual reads, and JSON/SQL reviews.
  • Search, hospital filtering, protected deletion, and dependent-record cleanup.
  • Populate, Test prerequisites, the ordered test, playback controls, and verified final records.
  • Automatic browser theme, manual dark/light overrides, refresh, and header links.

The recorder produces a complete overview plus separate chapter videos after a successful run. See the Dashboard guide for the full operating flow and field descriptions.

docs.title: Rebuild the supplied screenshot tour
docs.text:
Install FFmpeg on your PATH, then run from the repository root:

uv run --with pillow python docs/vid/render.py

The renderer reads timeline.json, pans/zooms its source image at the specified timestamps, adds captions, and writes walkthrough.mp4 and walkthrough.gif. Each file_path is relative to this folder. Optional crop and zoom_to boxes use [x, y, width, height] in source-image pixels. GIF inputs retain their frame delays. Rendering does not access the backend.

The first timestamp must be zero, later timestamps must increase, and duration must exceed the final timestamp. Crop boxes must stay within their source image. Use --timeline path/to/timeline.json for another recording.

docs.title: Record the live application
docs.text:
Start a fresh, uninitialized local FastAPI/MySQL instance. The recorder requires an empty database, operates the current UI, and does not use a mock API.

The recording writes to MySQL

It creates and edits walkthrough records, demonstrates protected deletion, removes temporary records, populates the baseline, and runs Test. It leaves the committed final state in the database. Use a disposable instance. bash run.sh -d deliberately deletes all project Compose volumes and data before starting.

Install FFmpeg and the optional capture tools:

uv run --with playwright --with pillow python -m playwright install chromium
uv run --with playwright --with pillow python docs/vid/capture.py --url http://localhost:3000

Add --headed to watch. For Vite, pass --url http://localhost:5173 with the API running on port 8080. Capture tools are not application dependencies.

On success, the recorder replaces the Overview tour, its timeline, the showcase page, and dashboard.png with the live recording. The README and docs home already reference that image; publication does not rewrite those pages. Original captures go into screens/, and the running-test GIF goes into clips/. It also renders one MP4/GIF/JSON per chapter. Capture and rendering use staging so a failure preserves previously published media; confirmed database writes remain committed.

The single-instance flow previews/cancels welcome Pre-populate, completes Start empty, and later confirms population through Testing. Independently recording a committed welcome Pre-populate choice requires another fresh instance.

To rebuild all chapters of a live recording, run:

uv run --with pillow python docs/vid/render.py --showcases

SQL previews are illustrative. The browser sends HTTP and JSON, never SQL; FastAPI executes parameterized ORM queries.
